issues.description: The declaration of ray_sphere_intersect in the template header omits the 'radius' parameter present in the implementation, causing a mismatch that will break compilation and confuse students about the required function signature. The solution repository and the template implementation expect a 'const float radius' parameter, but template's example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h declares only (const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template header declaration to match the implementation and solution by adding the radius parameter: change the prototype in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h to bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); This ensures consistent signatures across header and implementation and prevents compilation errors.

issues.description: The function 'ray_sphere_intersect' is declared with different parameter lists across artifacts: the template repository header declares only (origin, dir, center) while the implementation (cpp) and the solution repository header include an additional 'radius' parameter. This inconsistency in the function's signature (presence/absence of the 'radius' parameter) creates a conceptual and practical mismatch for students: the header they read does not match the implementation they must call or the solution reference, increasing confusion and leading to compile/link surprises.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the declaration and implementation: update the template header (example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h) to declare ray_sphere_intersect with the same parameters as the implementation and solution (const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius). This preserves the intended API and avoids student confusion.
